what_detected: The same timestamp appears twice in a sheet, or the timestamp cannot be parsed
why_wrong: A sensor reports once per instant, so a repeated timestamp is an export artefact
action: Keep the first row, drop the rest
alternatives_rejected: Averaging the duplicates: would invent a reading that no meter produced
evidence: Removed rows are counted per sensor in info['dropped_rows']
reversible: no - the row is not in the output

what_detected: Every electrical column is exactly 0 in every row of the sheet
why_wrong: A cumulative counter that never moves in five years is a disconnected meter, not a device that is off
action: Leave the sensor out of the output file entirely
alternatives_rejected: Keeping it as zeros: the model would learn five years of zero consumption as real
evidence: SE Projector: 61,689 rows, all five electrical columns exactly 0
reversible: no - the sensor is not in the output

what_detected: The median active power of the sensor is negative over the whole series
why_wrong: Lighting and sockets consume energy, they do not generate it; the current clamp is fitted backwards
action: Multiply W, I, Pa, Ea and Er by -1
alternatives_rejected: Deleting the sensor: would throw away 216,000 usable rows for a fault that is a sign flip
evidence: NW Emerg. Lighting: 99.3% of rows negative and the counter runs backwards (153031 -> 152900 -> 152769)

what_detected: Pa, W, I, Ea and Er are all exactly 0 in the same row
why_wrong: A cumulative counter cannot return to zero; the whole reading is missing and was written as zeros
action: Set all five to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Keeping the zeros: would create a huge negative then positive consumption in the counter difference
evidence: Zeros occur at the same timestamps across sheets, next to time gaps

what_detected: Ea or Er is exactly 0 in the middle of the series while power is normal
why_wrong: A cumulative counter only increases; a 0 mid-series is a missing value written as zero
action: Set the counter to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Interpolating immediately: the energy is recovered more accurately from the valid readings either side
evidence: Zeros cluster around data gaps rather than at low-consumption periods

what_detected: Ea or Er is below zero
why_wrong: A cumulative energy counter has no physical meaning below zero
action: Set the counter to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Absolute value: the magnitude of a corrupted counter carries no information
evidence: 82,101 negative counter cells across the four workbooks before cleaning

what_detected: A power or current value over 1,000x the typical magnitude, or 20x the 99.9th percentile
why_wrong: A circuit drawing 900 W cannot report 21 million W
action: Set the value to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Capping at the threshold: would invent a plausible-looking number in place of a known error
evidence: NW Plugs 2020-10-05 12:00: Pa = 2.1e7 W; that single row drags the W-Pa correlation from 0.93 to 0.01

what_detected: Pa, W or I is negative and its magnitude sits inside the sensor's normal range
why_wrong: These circuits only consume, so a negative reading is a sign error on an otherwise valid measurement
action: Replace with the absolute value
alternatives_rejected: Emptying it: discards a reading whose magnitude is clearly correct
evidence: W is active power, so every negative value on a consuming load is an error, not a capacitive effect

what_detected: Pa, W or I is negative and its magnitude would be an extreme outlier (above Q3 + 3 IQR)
why_wrong: Both the sign and the magnitude are wrong, so nothing in the reading can be trusted
action: Set the value to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Absolute value: would turn a corrupted reading into a false peak
evidence: Separating the two cases keeps 97,185 recoverable values while discarding only 99

what_detected: The counter drops below its level and returns to it within 24 hours
why_wrong: Each sheet sums up to 92 meters; when some do not answer, the total drops by their share and recovers when they return
action: Empty the affected readings; the energy is recovered from the valid readings on either side, so none is lost
alternatives_rejected: Absolute difference: would invent millions of Wh; interpolation: would hide the dropout instead of recording it
evidence: Negative counter steps fall from 12.0% to 0.1% after this rule; the share rises with meter count (Spearman 0.62)

what_detected: An isolated counter value far from its neighbours that the following readings do not confirm
why_wrong: A one-off jump with no lasting change is a transmission error, not a new meter level
action: Set the counter to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Treating it as a jump: would shift the whole counter baseline on the strength of one reading
evidence: Confirmed against the next 10 readings before deciding spike vs jump

what_detected: The counter drops and never returns to its previous level
why_wrong: The collector restored the counter to an earlier saved value; the reading is valid, the difference across it is not
action: Keep the value as a new valid level, but do not use the step across it as consumption
alternatives_rejected: Emptying it: the value is correct and later readings build on it
evidence: Resets hit up to 17 of 18 series at the same timestamp, so the cause is the platform, not the meters

what_detected: The counter rises more than the maximum power allows and the following readings confirm the new level
why_wrong: A genuine step change in the counter baseline, for example after a meter was replaced or reconfigured
action: Keep the value as a new valid level, but do not use the step across it as consumption
alternatives_rejected: Emptying it: would discard a correct reading and break every later difference
evidence: Confirmed only when the next 10 readings stay near the new level

what_detected: The counter is a partial sum in that row and the power is below 60% of its neighbours
why_wrong: When only some meters answer, the power columns are a partial sum too, not only the counter
action: Empty Pa, W and I for that row
alternatives_rejected: Keeping them: the model would see consumption collapsing for a minute and recovering, which never happened
evidence: Two independent columns agreeing (counter dips and power dips together) is a far more reliable signal than either alone

what_detected: A zero contradicted by another column: Pa = 0 while Ea rises, W = 0 while Er rises, or I = 0 with Pa above 5 W
why_wrong: If the energy counter advanced, the device was consuming, so the zero is a missing value
action: Set the value to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Keeping all zeros: would teach the model switch-offs that never happened and lower every average
evidence: NE HVAC: 89.9% of hourly rows have I = 0, and all of those have Pa above 5 W - a resolution floor, not a reading

what_detected: A high value (above Q3 + 3 IQR) confirmed by a second column or by the energy counter
why_wrong: A peak that several independent measurements agree on is a real event, such as a compressor starting
action: Keep the value, flag it only
alternatives_rejected: Removing or capping: real peaks are the most informative moments for a consumption model
evidence: Confirmation requires a second column in the 99th percentile, or the counter to have recorded that energy

what_detected: A high value that no other column in the same row supports
why_wrong: One quantity alone being extreme, with current and energy normal, is a measurement error
action: Set the value to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Winsorising at the threshold: would invent a number and erase the distinction from real peaks
evidence: Only upward outliers are treated; low values are real night and weekend periods the model must learn

what_detected: An environmental column is 0 in every row of the zone
why_wrong: A constant 0 degrees and 0% humidity indoors for five years means the sensor is absent or unconnected
action: Empty the whole column for that zone
alternatives_rejected: Loading it as zeros: would produce an average temperature of 0 degrees with no warning
evidence: Zone NE reports no environmental data at all: Lum, Hum, Temp and Pres are 0 in all 88,828 rows

what_detected: Humidity and temperature are both exactly 0 in the same row, or either is exactly 0 alone
why_wrong: 0 degrees C and 0% relative humidity are impossible in an occupied building; the reading is missing
action: Set the environmental values to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Keeping the zeros: would pull every environmental average towards zero
evidence: 508,949 zero cells across Temp and Hum before cleaning

what_detected: Temperature below -10 C or above 60 C
why_wrong: Outside this range the reading cannot come from an indoor sensor
action: Set the temperature to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: A narrower 10-35 C band: would delete 7,935 genuine cold readings, 6,571 of them in January 2021 (storm Filomena) - exactly the cold weather an energy model needs
evidence: SW records up to 1,411 C for one week, 1-7 March 2022: 534 rows, a contained sensor fault

what_detected: Humidity more than 5 points from the median of its neighbours over 3 hours, or outside 0-100%
why_wrong: Indoor humidity changes slowly, so a single reading far from its neighbours is a sensor step
action: Set the humidity to empty (NaN), then fill it if the gap is short
alternatives_rejected: Keeping it: single-reading spikes would be learned as real humidity events
evidence: Hum has only 19 distinct integer values in 1.3M rows, so its resolution is already low

what_detected: Pres holds a value other than 0 or 1
why_wrong: Pres is a presence detector, not the atmospheric pressure the column name suggests, so only 0 and 1 are valid
action: Set the value to empty (NaN)
alternatives_rejected: Rescaling to a pressure: the column has only ever contained 0 and 1, so there is nothing to rescale
evidence: At 1-minute resolution NW and SE show a clean occupancy curve (0.00 overnight, peak 0.238 at 11:00 UTC) with a median run of 2 minutes - a motion sensor, not a pressure

what_detected: A gap of at most 15 minutes in Pa, W, I, Hum or Temp
why_wrong: These quantities change continuously, so a short gap can be bridged without inventing a trend
action: Fill linearly between the valid readings either side
alternatives_rejected: Filling long gaps: would invent data; filling Lum or Pres: both change abruptly and Pres is binary
evidence: The limit is set in hours and converted per sampling regime, so it means 15 minutes in both eras

what_detected: Active power exceeds apparent power (W > Pa)
why_wrong: Active power cannot exceed apparent power for a single meter (P <= S)
action: Flag the row, change nothing
alternatives_rejected: Correcting either column: the data cannot say which of the two is wrong, so any fix would be a guess
evidence: 0.52% of rows overall, concentrated in SE Lighting (7.8%); these columns are sums over up to 92 meters, so the per-meter bound need not hold on the total
